summary: EMMIR is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in migration studies, run by eight universities in Europe, Africa and Asia, including the University of Ghana in Accra. You start at the University of Oldenburg in Germany, spend the second semester at the University of Stavanger in Norway, and choose a partner for the third. A very limited number of scholarships pay €1,400 a month for 24 months. Apply by 20 December 2026.
meta_title: EMMIR 2027: Erasmus Mundus migration master's scholarship
meta_description: EMMIR pays €1,400 a month for 24 months plus fees for a migration master's in Germany, Norway, Ghana, Uganda and beyond. Apply by 20 December 2026.
covers: Health insurance, university registration and student service fees.
There are no separate travel or installation payments: travel, visas, vaccinations and residence permits come out of the monthly stipend.
eligibility: A first degree, such as a bachelor's, in a field related to migration studies, with a final grade of at least C+ and no more than five years old.
To apply for a scholarship, the degree must be completed by 20 December 2026. EMMIR makes no exceptions.
Relevant professional experience is preferred. Anyone who has held an Erasmus Mundus scholarship before cannot get another.
how_to_apply: Apply online for Edition 14 (2027–2029). Applications opened on 1 October 2026.
Upload as PDFs your passport, CV, a one- to two-page statement of purpose, your degree certificate and transcript, and your English documents.
Submit by 20 December 2026, 23:59 CET. The selection board meets at the end of March 2027 and tells applicants in April.
If you are admitted, send the signed application and certified copies of your documents within 10 calendar days.
watch_out: You do not need an English test if you come from a country where English is an official language. Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya, Uganda and South Africa are on EMMIR's list.
The first semester is in Oldenburg, Germany, where non-scholarship students must show €11,208 in a blocked account for the first year.

Third-semester partners include the University of Ghana, Mbarara University of Science and Technology in Uganda, the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, Charles University in Prague and the University of Nova Gorica.
Self-funded students who pay fees are charged €4,500 a semester.
documents: Statement of purpose, one to two pages
English proficiency documents or proof of exemption

faq.q: When is the EMMIR scholarship deadline?
faq.a: 20 December 2026 at 23:59 CET, for Edition 14, which starts on 1 September 2027.

faq.q: Is the University of Ghana part of EMMIR?
faq.a: Yes. The University of Ghana's Centre for Migration Studies joined the consortium as a partner in 2026.
No. Travel and visa costs come out of the €1,400 monthly stipend.
